subject: Animation
title: Osamu Tezuka: The God of Manga
description: A short lesson to help you apply Osamu Tezuka: The God of Manga.

hook.text: Osamu Tezuka drew his first manga at age 17 and would go on to create over 700 works in his lifetime.

buildup.text: He introduced cinematic storytelling to manga with dramatic angles, pacing, and emotional depth.

discovery.text: Tezuka's Astro Boy became the first major anime TV series in 1963, launching an entire industry.

twist.text: He set production budgets so low that the anime industry still grapples with overwork decades later.

climax.text: Tezuka's influence on both manga and anime is so vast that Japan calls him the God of Manga.

punchline.text: One artist shaped an entire nation's storytelling culture.

quiz.question: Why is Osamu Tezuka called the God of Manga?
options: He invented the printing press in Japan
He pioneered cinematic manga storytelling and launched the anime industry with Astro Boy
He was the first Japanese artist to work in Hollywood

details.summary: Osamu Tezuka created the visual language of modern manga and anime: large expressive eyes, dynamic panel layouts, and cinematic storytelling. His prolific output and artistic innovation earned him the title 'God of Manga' and shaped the entire medium.
details.whyItMatters: Virtually every manga and anime created since the 1950s exists in a tradition Tezuka established. Understanding Tezuka means understanding the DNA of an art form that now generates billions in global revenue.
takeaways: Tezuka created the foundational visual language of manga and anime
His large-eye character style became anime's most recognizable trait
He is considered the single most important figure in manga history

faq.question: Why did Tezuka draw characters with large eyes?
faq.answer: Tezuka was influenced by Disney and Betty Boop cartoons. He adopted large eyes to convey emotion expressively. This style became anime's signature visual trait, copied by virtually every manga artist who followed.

faq.question: What were Tezuka's most important works?
faq.answer: Astro Boy defined robot manga. Kimba the White Lion pioneered animal drama. Black Jack explored medical ethics. Phoenix is his philosophical masterwork. He created over 700 manga volumes spanning every conceivable genre.
